fun_facts: Poha absorbs less oil during cooking than rice, making it naturally lighter.
A plate of poha has roughly the same calories as 1.5 slices of bread.
The iron content in poha is surprisingly high because of the flattening process.
common_mistakes: People underestimate because it looks light and fluffy, but oil and peanuts add up.
visual_references: 1 katori = roughly a cricket ball volume = ~180 cal

fried idli / idli fry.note: Deep frying absorbs oil — fat jumps dramatically (0.3g base), protein/carbs barely change

fun_facts: A plain idli is one of the lowest calorie Indian breakfast items at just 52 calories each.
Idli batter fermentation creates probiotics that aid digestion.
The real calorie trap isn't the idli — it's the ghee and chutneys.
common_mistakes: People forget to count the accompaniments. 4 idli + sambar + chutney is ~350 cal, not 200.
visual_references: 1 idli = roughly the size of a hockey puck = ~52 cal

mysore masala dosa.note: Red chutney spread + potato + extra oil

set dosa.note: Smaller, thicker, less oil per piece

fun_facts: A restaurant masala dosa can have 350-400 calories — nearly as much as a McDonald's burger.
The difference between a home dosa and restaurant dosa can be 100+ calories purely from oil.
Rava dosa uses more oil to get crispy, despite seeming 'lighter'.
common_mistakes: Masala dosa is the classic underestimate. People think ~200 cal when it's closer to 350-400 with accompaniments.
visual_references: 1 regular dosa = roughly the area of a dinner plate = ~190 cal plain

rumali roti.note: Paper thin, lower cal per piece

fun_facts: The size of roti varies hugely — a dhaba roti can be 2x the calories of a home roti.
Adding ghee to each roti adds up fast: 3 rotis with ghee = extra 100+ calories vs dry.
Phulka (puffed roti) and chapati are the same thing — phulka just puffs on direct flame.
common_mistakes: People count rotis but forget the ghee. 3 rotis 'with a little ghee' can be 400+ cal.
visual_references: 1 medium roti = roughly the size of a standard plate rim = ~100 cal

jeera rice.note: Ghee + cumin tempering adds fat to nearly-zero-fat rice

fried rice.note: Significant oil added to low-fat base

fun_facts: A fist-sized portion of cooked rice is roughly 130 calories.
Most people eat 1.5-2 fists of rice without realizing it — that's 200-260 cal before any curry.
Brown rice has only 10-15% fewer calories than white rice — the real difference is fiber.
common_mistakes: The biggest rice mistake is portion blindness. People pour rice without measuring and often eat 300g+ thinking it was 'one serving'.
visual_references: 1 closed fist = ~100g cooked rice = ~130 cal

dal makhani.note: Butter + cream makes it very rich in fat

fun_facts: Plain boiled dal is very low calorie and high protein — one of the best Indian diet foods.
Dal makhani at a restaurant can have 2-3x the calories of home-cooked tadka dal.
The tadka (tempering) alone can add 50-80 calories to a bowl of dal.
common_mistakes: Dal makhani is the classic trap. It sounds healthy ('it's just dal') but restaurant versions are loaded with butter and cream.
visual_references: 1 katori of dal = roughly a tennis ball volume = ~110 cal for tadka dal

fun_facts: A restaurant butter chicken with 2 naans can easily be 900-1000 calories for one meal.
The 'butter' in butter chicken is real — a restaurant portion can have 3-4 tablespoons of butter.
Switching from butter chicken to tandoori chicken saves about 150-200 calories per serving.
common_mistakes: People guess ~300 cal for a restaurant serving when it's closer to 400-500 for the gravy alone.
visual_references: 1 restaurant bowl = roughly 250ml = ~375 cal

restaurant style.note: Heavy on cream and cashew paste

fun_facts: Paneer itself is 265 cal per 100g — it's one of the most calorie-dense vegetarian proteins.
A restaurant paneer butter masala can match a butter chicken in calories.
People assume vegetarian = lighter, but paneer curries are often MORE calorie-dense than chicken curries.
common_mistakes: The 'vegetarian is lighter' fallacy. Paneer butter masala is often 450-550 cal per serving.
visual_references: 6 cubes of paneer (100g) = roughly 265 cal before any gravy

fun_facts: A Swiggy single-serve biryani is often 700-800 calories — nearly half a day's intake.
The ghee layered between rice layers is what makes biryani calorie-dense vs plain rice + chicken.
Hyderabadi biryani tends to be richer than Lucknowi because of the dum cooking with more fat.
common_mistakes: Biryani is the most commonly underestimated Indian dish. People guess 400 when a Swiggy portion is 700-800.
visual_references: A standard delivery biryani container = ~400-450g = 700-800 cal

fun_facts: 2 regular samosas = about 500 calories, roughly the same as a full meal.
The outer pastry shell absorbs a LOT of oil during frying — that's where most calories hide.
A baked samosa has about 30% fewer calories than a fried one.
common_mistakes: 'It's just a snack' — but 2 samosas with chutney = 550+ cal.
visual_references: 1 regular samosa = roughly the size of your palm = ~250 cal

with butter on top.note: The classic Punjabi finish — extra 50 cal

fun_facts: 2 aloo parathas with butter and curd = 750-800 calories. That's a full meal's worth at breakfast.
A restaurant paratha uses 2-3x more ghee/oil than a home-cooked one.
The stuffing matters less than you think — the real calories are in the dough layers and cooking fat.
common_mistakes: People focus on the stuffing (aloo vs gobhi) but ignore the ghee/butter. A 'light' gobhi paratha with extra butter = same as aloo.
visual_references: 1 aloo paratha = roughly a dinner plate diameter = ~310 cal

cheese naan.note: Cheese adds both protein and fat

fun_facts: One butter naan has about 320 calories — nearly as much as a full plate of rice.
Most people eat 2-3 naans with a curry, adding 600-900 calories just from bread.
Naan uses maida (refined flour), yogurt, and oil in the dough — it's richer than roti by default.
common_mistakes: Naan vs roti: people think they're similar, but one naan = 2.5 to 3 rotis in calories.
visual_references: 1 naan = roughly the size of a large hand spread = ~260 cal plain

chole bhature combo.note: Bhatura alone is 300+ cal. Full combo = 600-700

fun_facts: Chole alone is actually quite healthy — high protein, high fiber. The problem is what you eat it WITH.
A chole bhature plate at a dhaba can be 700-800 calories total.
Chickpeas are one of the best plant protein sources at ~19g protein per 100g dry.
common_mistakes: Chole bhature: people think of it as one dish but it's really 250 cal (chole) + 350 cal (bhatura) + oil.
visual_references: 1 katori chole = tennis ball volume = ~180 cal

fun_facts: Street-side pav bhaji uses an obscene amount of butter — some vendors use a quarter block per plate.
The pav (bread) alone is ~150 cal per piece. Most plates come with 2-3 pavs.
The bhaji is mostly vegetables and is the healthier part — it's the butter and pav that add up.
common_mistakes: 'It's just vegetables and bread' — a street pav bhaji plate can be 600-700 calories.
visual_references: 1 street plate = ~550-650 cal with standard 2 pav

standard.note: Fried vada in pav with chutneys

fun_facts: A vada pav has about the same calories as a McDonald's McAloo Tikki burger.
It's called the 'Indian burger' for good reason — similar calorie density too.
The deep-fried vada absorbs a lot of oil. That's where 40% of the calories come from.
common_mistakes: Seems like a small snack, but at 290 cal each, 2 vada pavs = a full meal's calories.
visual_references: 1 vada pav = roughly the size of a tennis ball in a bun = ~290 cal

fun_facts: Upma and poha have very similar calories — upma just feels heavier because semolina is denser.
The oil used for tempering can account for 25-30% of upma's total calories.
common_mistakes: Upma seems lighter than poha but it's about the same. The semolina + oil tempering is calorie-comparable.
visual_references: 1 plate upma = roughly the same as 1 plate poha = ~300 cal

fun_facts: Rajma is one of the best plant protein sources — 24g protein per 100g dry beans.
Rajma chawal is a complete protein meal — the rice and beans together provide all essential amino acids.
A full rajma chawal plate (bowl of rajma + plate of rice) = about 550-650 calories.
common_mistakes: People estimate rajma and rice separately and still get it wrong. The combo is 550-650 cal.
visual_references: 1 katori rajma = tennis ball = ~165 cal; add 1 plate rice = 425 total

with milk + 2 tsp sugar.note: Extra sugar adds ~20 cal per tsp

fun_facts: 3-4 cups of regular chai per day = 200-350 extra calories that most people don't count.
The sugar in chai is the hidden calorie bomb. Each teaspoon adds ~20 calories.
A cutting chai from a tapri is one of the lowest-calorie warm beverages at just 30 cal.
common_mistakes: Nobody counts chai calories. 4 cups/day with 2 tsp sugar each = 300+ invisible calories.
visual_references: 1 regular cup = ~55 cal; cutting chai = ~30 cal

fun_facts: Each gulab jamun is a calorie triple threat: deep fried dough + soaked in sugar syrup + made from khoya (reduced milk).
2 gulab jamuns = 260 calories, roughly the same as a full bowl of dal chawal.
The sugar syrup alone accounts for about 40% of the calories.
common_mistakes: They're small so people eat 3-4. That's 400-500 calories of pure sugar and fat.
visual_references: 1 gulab jamun = roughly the size of a golf ball = ~130 cal

standard.note: Deep fried and sugar syrup soaked

fun_facts: Jalebi is one of the most calorie-dense Indian sweets at 380 cal per 100g.
A small plate of jalebi with rabri can be 500+ calories — basically a full meal.
The deep frying + sugar syrup soak is a calorie double hit.
common_mistakes: They look light and airy, but each jalebi ring is soaked in sugar syrup and fried. 3 pieces = 300+ cal.
visual_references: 1 jalebi ring = ~115 cal; a standard plate = ~300 cal

fun_facts: Each tiny pani puri is about 40 calories. A standard serving of 6 = 240 calories.
The puri shell is deep fried — that's where most calories hide, not the water filling.
Nobody stops at 6. A typical street-side session of 10-12 puris = 400-500 calories.
common_mistakes: 'It's just water and a tiny shell' — but 10 puris = 400 cal, mainly from the fried shells.
visual_references: 1 pani puri = ping pong ball size = ~40 cal each

fun_facts: A single Maggi pack is 310 calories — not terrible for a snack, but most people cook two packs.
60% of Maggi's calories come from the noodle block (fried before packaging), not the masala.
Hostel Maggi with butter, cheese, and egg can hit 500+ calories easily.
common_mistakes: Double pack Maggi is 620 cal — that's a full meal but most people eat it AS a snack on top of meals.
visual_references: 1 pack cooked = roughly a large bowl = ~310 cal

fun_facts: Egg bhurji is one of the best protein-to-calorie ratios in Indian street food.
2-egg bhurji with light oil = 200 cal with 14g protein. Hard to beat that.
The street-side anda pav version doubles the calories because of the buttered pav.
common_mistakes: The bhurji itself is fine. It's the 2 buttered pavs that turn a 200-cal snack into 500 cal.
visual_references: 2-egg bhurji = roughly half a plate = ~200 cal

mango.note: Mango pulp adds carbs/sugar, not fat

fun_facts: A Punjabi tall glass sweet lassi = 280 cal. That's a liquid meal people drink alongside their actual meal.
Switching from sweet to salted lassi saves 100+ calories per glass.
Mango lassi at restaurants often uses sugar AND mango pulp — double sweetness, 200+ cal.
common_mistakes: Beverages don't register as 'food' mentally. A tall lassi adds 280 cal to a meal without feeling like it.
visual_references: 1 regular glass = ~175 cal sweet; ~70 cal salted

fun_facts: Aloo gobi is one of the lighter curries — if it's not deep-fried first.
The difference between a home-cooked and restaurant aloo gobi can be 50-70% more calories due to oil.
Cauliflower is only 25 cal/100g. The potato and oil are doing all the calorie work.
common_mistakes: Restaurant versions often deep-fry the cauliflower first, which almost doubles the calories vs. home-cooked.
visual_references: 1 katori = ~145 cal homemade — a lighter curry option

fun_facts: The spinach (palak) in palak paneer is practically zero calories. It's the paneer and cream doing the heavy lifting.
100g of paneer = 265 calories. A standard portion of palak paneer has about 100-150g of paneer in it.
Switching to tofu instead of paneer saves about 40% calories.
common_mistakes: 'Green = healthy' — but the paneer and cream make this a 350+ cal dish per restaurant bowl.
visual_references: 1 katori = ~210 cal; restaurant bowl = ~350 cal

fun_facts: A medium banana is ~105 cal. It's one of the easiest food items to remember for calibration.
Banana is the gold standard reference food: if you can estimate a banana, you can estimate most fruits.
A banana shake with full cream milk and sugar = 250-300 cal. The banana is the least of it.
common_mistakes: People often think bananas are higher calorie than they are. A medium banana = just 105 cal.
visual_references: 1 medium banana = ~105 cal — use this as your mental calibration anchor

fun_facts: Each medu vada absorbs a surprising amount of oil during frying — about 15-20% of its weight.
Medu vada with sambar is often healthier than it looks because urad dal is high in protein.
The crispy outside and soft inside texture means the outer layer is where most oil (and calories) hide.
common_mistakes: People undercount because they're small. 3 vadas with sambar = 450 cal — a full meal.
visual_references: 1 medu vada = roughly a small donut size = ~135 cal

fun_facts: Uttapam uses more oil than a regular dosa because it sits on the pan longer and is thicker.
Despite being thicker than a dosa, uttapam often has fewer calories because there is no potato filling.
common_mistakes: Thicker than dosa so people assume double the calories, but it's only about 40-50% more.
visual_references: 1 regular uttapam = roughly a small plate = ~280 cal

fun_facts: Tandoori chicken is one of the best protein-to-calorie ratios in Indian food — about 25g protein per piece.
Switching from butter chicken to tandoori saves 150-200 calories per serving with more protein.
The red color comes from Kashmiri chili and food color, not from extra oil.
common_mistakes: People overestimate because it looks rich, but tandoori is actually one of the leanest Indian preparations.
visual_references: 1 leg piece = ~180 cal with 22g protein — great macro ratio

fun_facts: Chicken tikka is essentially high-protein, low-carb — ideal for anyone tracking macros.
6 pieces of tikka have more protein than a glass of whey shake, at similar calories.
common_mistakes: Chicken tikka vs chicken tikka MASALA: tikka is 200 cal, tikka masala is 400+ cal. The gravy doubles it.
visual_references: 6 tikka pieces = roughly a fist = ~200 cal with 25g protein

fun_facts: Paneer tikka has nearly 30% more calories than chicken tikka for the same weight.
Paneer is 265 cal per 100g vs chicken breast at 165 cal per 100g — vegetarian protein is calorie-expensive.
common_mistakes: Assuming paneer tikka is 'lighter' because it's grilled. Paneer is inherently calorie-dense at 265/100g.
visual_references: 6 paneer cubes = roughly 100g = ~265 cal

fun_facts: Egg curry is one of the most protein-efficient Indian curries — 2 eggs give you 12-14g protein.
A boiled egg is only 70 cal. The gravy adds about 90 cal. Together it is still a lean curry.
common_mistakes: Egg curry is lighter than most people think. The eggs are lean and the gravy is typically not cream-based.
visual_references: 2-egg curry = ~230 cal — one of the lightest curries

fish fry + curry.note: Fried fish in curry is much richer

fun_facts: Fish curry is one of the lowest calorie protein-rich Indian dishes.
Kerala-style fish curry with coconut is 30% more calories than a tamarind-based one.
common_mistakes: Fish is lean but coconut-based curry adds significantly. Kerala fish curry is not the same as Goan fish curry in calories.
visual_references: 1 piece fish curry = ~210 cal — excellent protein-to-calorie ratio

fun_facts: Plain kadhi without pakoras is one of the lowest calorie Indian curries at just 105 cal per katori.
The pakoras in kadhi pakora can double the calorie count. It is the fried bits, not the yogurt.
common_mistakes: Kadhi without pakoras vs with pakoras is a 2x calorie difference. Always check which version.
visual_references: 1 katori plain kadhi = ~105 cal — great light curry option

fun_facts: Khichdi is considered a 'sick day food' but it is actually well-balanced — complete protein from rice + dal.
Plain khichdi is surprisingly moderate in calories. It is the ghee on top that changes everything.
common_mistakes: Khichdi seems light but a plate with generous ghee hits 350 cal — the ghee is invisible but significant.
visual_references: 1 plate plain khichdi = ~290 cal; with ghee = ~350 cal

vegetable pulao.note: Rice cooked with veggies and spices in oil

egg fried rice.note: More oil, egg adds protein and calories

fun_facts: Pulao sits between plain rice and biryani in calories — more than steamed rice, less than biryani.
The oil used to cook the rice and temper spices adds about 40-60 cal over plain steamed rice.
common_mistakes: People treat pulao as 'just rice' but the cooking oil makes it 40-50% more caloric than plain steamed rice.
visual_references: 1 plate pulao = ~365 cal vs plain rice at ~260 cal

fun_facts: Bhel puri is actually one of the lighter street food options — puffed rice is very low density.
A plate of bhel puri has about half the calories of a plate of pani puri because less is deep fried.
common_mistakes: Bhel puri is lighter than it looks. The puffed rice base is very low calorie — most calories come from sev and chutneys.
visual_references: 1 regular plate = ~215 cal — one of the lightest street food options

fun_facts: A kathi roll is basically a paratha wrapped around a filling — the paratha alone is 200+ cal.
The roll wrapping is what makes it calorie-heavy. The filling is often the lighter part.
common_mistakes: Kathi rolls seem like a light meal but the paratha wrap is 200+ cal before any filling.
visual_references: 1 chicken roll = ~420 cal — it is a full meal, not a snack

fried.note: Frying adds fat, not much else

tandoori momos.note: Sauce and cooking method add calories

fun_facts: Steamed momos are actually fairly reasonable at 40 cal each. It is when they are fried that calories jump 50%.
The mayo-based dipping sauce can add 100-150 cal to your plate without you noticing.
common_mistakes: Fried momos vs steamed momos is a 50% calorie jump. And the mayo dip adds another 100-150 cal.
visual_references: 6 steamed momos = ~240 cal; 6 fried momos = ~360 cal

fun_facts: Pakoras are basically vegetables dipped in batter and deep fried. The besan batter absorbs a LOT of oil.
A rainy day plate of chai + pakoras can easily be 400+ calories as a 'snack'.
common_mistakes: They are small so you keep eating. 10 pakoras = 360 cal without even feeling full.
visual_references: 5 pakoras = roughly a handful = ~180 cal

fun_facts: Kachori is even more calorie-dense than samosa per gram because the filling is usually dal or onion mixed with oil.
A breakfast of 2 kachoris with sabzi can be 600-700 calories.
common_mistakes: Kachori looks similar to samosa but is often denser and higher calorie per piece.
visual_references: 1 regular kachori = ~250 cal — denser than a samosa

fun_facts: A plain aloo tikki is only about 120 cal. The chaat toppings can add 200+ more.
McDonalds McAloo Tikki is basically this concept with a bun — about 340 cal.
common_mistakes: Plain tikki vs tikki chaat is a massive difference. The chutneys, curd, and sev add 150+ calories.
visual_references: 1 tikki = palm-sized patty = ~120 cal plain

rasmalai.note: Flattened in sweetened milk — much richer

fun_facts: Rasgulla is one of the lighter Indian sweets at just 75 cal per piece — about half of gulab jamun.
Unlike gulab jamun, rasgulla is NOT fried. It is boiled in sugar syrup, which makes it significantly lighter.
common_mistakes: People lump all Indian sweets together. Rasgulla is 75 cal vs gulab jamun at 130 cal — almost half.
visual_references: 1 rasgulla = spongy golf ball = ~75 cal

fun_facts: Ladoos are calorie bombs because they are made of ghee + sugar + flour — the three most calorie-dense ingredients.
One medium besan ladoo has the same calories as 2 rotis.
common_mistakes: They are small and round so you pop one casually. But 1 medium ladoo = 200 cal = 2 rotis.
visual_references: 1 medium ladoo = slightly larger than a golf ball = ~200 cal

fun_facts: Kheer gets most of its calories from the reduced milk (rabri base) and sugar, not the rice.
A small bowl of kheer after a meal adds 140 calories — the same as an extra roti.
common_mistakes: Kheer seems liquid and light, but reduced milk is calorie-dense. A regular bowl = 250 cal.
visual_references: 1 regular bowl = ~250 cal — treat it as a calorie-dense addition

fun_facts: Filter coffee is slightly higher calorie than chai because it typically uses more milk.
3 filter coffees a day = 200+ invisible calories, similar to chai.
common_mistakes: Like chai, people forget to count coffee calories. 3 per day = 200+ cal from beverages alone.
visual_references: 1 tumbler = ~70 cal — similar to chai

with malai (coconut flesh).note: The flesh is very calorie dense

fun_facts: Coconut water is one of the lowest calorie natural beverages at just 57 cal per tender coconut.
The malai (flesh) is where all the calories hide — it can triple the calorie count.
common_mistakes: Coconut water = 57 cal. Coconut water with all the malai = 180 cal. Big difference.
visual_references: 1 tender coconut water = ~57 cal — very light

plain salted.note: Diluted curd with salt and spices

fun_facts: Buttermilk is the lowest calorie Indian beverage choice at just 50 cal per glass.
Chaas vs sweet lassi: 50 cal vs 175 cal — same base ingredient, very different calorie load.
common_mistakes: People confuse chaas with lassi. Chaas is diluted and salted (50 cal), lassi is concentrated and sweetened (175 cal).
visual_references: 1 glass chaas = ~50 cal — the lightest Indian beverage

fun_facts: One bhatura alone has about the same calories as 2.5 rotis.
Bhatura is made from maida (refined flour) and deep fried — the worst combination for calorie density.
common_mistakes: In chole bhature, people blame the chole. But the bhatura is 256 cal, the chole is only 180 cal.
visual_references: 1 bhatura = large puffed balloon = ~256 cal

fun_facts: Each poori is small but at 73 cal each, eating 4-5 pooris (common) = 300-365 cal just from bread.
Poori vs roti: poori is deep fried so each piece has 1.5x the calories of a similar-sized roti.
common_mistakes: They are small so you eat many. 5 pooris = 365 cal. Most people eat 4-6 without thinking.
visual_references: 1 poori = small puffed disc = ~73 cal each

fun_facts: Dal chawal is a complete protein meal — rice + lentils together provide all essential amino acids.
A simple dal chawal is about 370 cal — one of the most balanced and moderate Indian meals.
common_mistakes: Dal chawal is moderate but people often underestimate the rice portion. Most serve 200g+ rice.
visual_references: Standard dal chawal = ~370 cal — benchmark for a moderate Indian meal

fun_facts: A boiled egg is 70 cal with 6g protein — one of the best protein-per-calorie foods available.
Boiled vs fried: 70 cal vs 100 cal per egg. The cooking method adds 30+ calories.
common_mistakes: Boiled egg = 70 cal. Fried egg = 100 cal. Omelette with oil = 100 cal. Method matters.
visual_references: 1 boiled egg = ~70 cal / 6g protein — your protein calibration anchor

with tempering.note: Mustard, curry leaf tadka adds some

fun_facts: Curd rice is one of the lightest rice preparations because the curd dilutes the calorie density.
South Indians often eat curd rice as the last course. At 165 cal per katori, it is a sensible way to end a meal.
common_mistakes: Curd rice feels heavy but is actually lighter than most rice dishes because curd replaces oil/ghee.
visual_references: 1 katori curd rice = ~165 cal — lighter than you think

fun_facts: Rasam is one of the lowest calorie Indian dishes at just 28 cal/100g — almost like flavored water.
A full bowl of rasam has fewer calories than a single idli.
common_mistakes: Rasam is basically negligible calories. The rice you eat it with is where the calories are.
visual_references: 1 bowl rasam = ~70 cal — the lightest curry you can eat

fun_facts: Sambar is a complete nutritional package — lentils for protein, vegetables for fiber, at just 50 cal/100g.
The vegetables in sambar (drumstick, okra, gourd) are almost zero-calorie themselves.
common_mistakes: Sambar itself is light. But people pour it over a mountain of rice and blame the sambar.
visual_references: 1 katori sambar = ~75 cal with decent protein from dal

fun_facts: Avial gets most of its calories from coconut, not the vegetables.
A katori of avial has about the same calories as one idli.
common_mistakes: It looks like a vegetable dish but coconut paste makes it richer than it appears.
visual_references: 1 katori = ~90 cal — moderate for a veggie dish due to coconut

with stew.note: Stew is separate, ~80 cal per katori

fun_facts: Appam is lacy and thin at the edges but thick in the center — the center is where most calories concentrate.
The fermentation in appam batter actually improves nutrient absorption.
common_mistakes: One appam looks small but at 110 cal each, 3 appams + stew = 450+ cal.
visual_references: 1 appam = bowl-shaped pancake = ~110 cal

ragi puttu.note: Finger millet base, slightly lower cal

fun_facts: One full puttu cylinder can be 345 calories — almost as much as a plate of rice.
The coconut layers in puttu contribute most of the fat content.
common_mistakes: Puttu with banana and sugar for breakfast can be 500+ calories before you leave the house.
visual_references: 1 puttu cylinder = ~345 cal — surprisingly calorie-dense

fun_facts: Pongal is essentially rice-dal khichdi's South Indian cousin — similar calories but with more ghee.
The cashews and ghee in pongal contribute 30-40% of its total calories.
common_mistakes: Pongal looks like a simple porridge but the ghee makes it 30% more caloric than plain khichdi.
visual_references: 1 plate pongal = ~325 cal — heavier than it looks

dry.note: Deep fried balls with sauce coating

gravy.note: Gravy adds water, dilutes per-100g density

fun_facts: Veg Manchurian is essentially deep-fried vegetable balls — the 'Chinese' tag makes people forget it is fried.
A Manchurian + fried rice combo can hit 600 calories easily.
common_mistakes: Manchurian + fried rice is treated as one dish but it is really two calorie-heavy items together.
visual_references: 1 plate dry manchurian = ~263 cal — mostly from deep frying

standard.note: Rice stir-fried with veggies and soy sauce

egg fried rice.note: Egg adds protein and some fat

fun_facts: Fried rice has 30% more calories than steamed rice per 100g — all from the cooking oil.
A full plate of fried rice (250g) = 430 cal, vs steamed rice at 325 cal for the same amount.
common_mistakes: People think 'just rice with vegetables' but the frying oil adds 100+ calories per plate.
visual_references: 1 plate fried rice = ~430 cal vs steamed rice plate ~325 cal

dry.note: Battered fried chicken with peppers and sauce

fun_facts: Chilli chicken has decent protein (16g/100g) but the batter and frying add significant fat.
Dry chilli chicken vs tandoori chicken: same protein, but chilli chicken has 3x the fat.
common_mistakes: It is chicken so it must be healthy — but the batter coating and deep frying change everything.
visual_references: 1 plate dry chilli chicken = ~293 cal with 24g protein

fun_facts: Hakka noodles are lighter than fried rice per 100g because noodles absorb less oil.
A plate of noodles is about the same calories as a plate of biryani.
common_mistakes: Noodles seem lighter than rice but a full plate is still 325 cal.
visual_references: 1 plate hakka noodles = ~325 cal

fun_facts: Two pizza slices (570 cal) equals roughly a butter chicken + naan meal.
Thin crust saves about 15% calories vs regular crust — the dough is the biggest calorie contributor.
common_mistakes: People eat 3-4 slices thinking it is one meal. That is 850-1140 cal.
visual_references: 1 pizza slice = ~285 cal — about the same as a vada pav

double patty.note: Extra patty nearly doubles the filling

fun_facts: A basic burger has almost the same calories as a vada pav per 100g.
The bun alone contributes about 150 calories to a standard burger.
common_mistakes: Adding cheese and mayo can push a 430 cal burger to 600+ cal. The add-ons are not free.
visual_references: 1 regular burger = ~430 cal — similar to chole bhature

white/alfredo.note: Cream sauce nearly doubles the fat

pesto.note: Oil and nuts in pesto add calories

fun_facts: Pasta with tomato sauce is actually one of the lighter international options at 140 cal/100g.
White sauce pasta can be 60% more calories than red sauce — cream is the culprit.
common_mistakes: Red vs white sauce is a 200+ calorie difference per plate. Always check which sauce.
visual_references: 1 plate red sauce pasta = ~350 cal; white sauce = ~560 cal

fun_facts: French fries at 312 cal/100g are more calorie-dense than samosas (308 cal/100g).
A large fries serving is 468 calories — more than a full plate of dal chawal.
common_mistakes: Fries are treated as a side dish but a large serving has more calories than many full meals.
visual_references: Medium fries = ~365 cal — basically a meal's worth

fun_facts: Dhokla is one of the healthiest Indian snacks at 145 cal/100g — steaming keeps fat minimal.
4 pieces of dhokla have fewer calories than 1 samosa.
common_mistakes: Dhokla is genuinely light. The issue is the sugar in some Gujarati versions and the oil tempering on top.
visual_references: 4 pieces = ~174 cal — one of the lightest snack options

fun_facts: Thepla is basically a flavored paratha — similar calorie profile but with added fenugreek nutrition.
3 theplas with pickle is a common travel meal at 360+ calories.
common_mistakes: They are thin so people eat 3-4. At 120 cal each, that is 360-480 cal from bread alone.
visual_references: 1 thepla = ~120 cal — similar to 1 roti with ghee

standard deep fried.note: Rice flour + urad dal, deep fried

fun_facts: Murukku at 470 cal/100g is the most calorie-dense snack in our entire database.
A small bowl of murukku has more calories than a plate of biryani.
common_mistakes: They are crunchy and addictive. A handful (60g) is 282 calories without even realizing.
visual_references: Small bowl of murukku = ~376 cal — extremely calorie dense

fun_facts: A large cold coffee with ice cream (385 cal) has more calories than a plate of chole chawal.
Without ice cream, cold coffee drops to about 165 cal per glass — a 60% reduction.
common_mistakes: It is a beverage so people do not count it. But a glass of cold coffee can be 275-385 calories.
visual_references: 1 glass with ice cream = ~275 cal — a liquid meal

fun_facts: Mango lassi has double the calories of regular sweet lassi because of the mango pulp sugar.
A tall glass of mango lassi (300 cal) consumed alongside a meal can add 25% to your total intake.
common_mistakes: Lassi feels like a drink but at 188-300 cal per glass, it is really a dessert.
visual_references: 1 glass mango lassi = ~188 cal — treat it as food, not just a drink

with honey.note: Honey adds slightly more cal than sugar

fun_facts: Nimbu pani without sugar is basically zero calories — all the calories come from sugar.
Switching from a sweet lassi to nimbu pani saves 100+ calories per glass.
common_mistakes: Without sugar it is 10 cal. With sugar it is 75 cal. Same drink, very different numbers.
visual_references: 1 glass with sugar = ~75 cal; without sugar = ~10 cal

with milk.note: Milk adds protein, carbs, and fat

fun_facts: Plain oats in water is just 68 cal/100g — one of the lowest calorie breakfast bases.
But oats with milk, honey, banana, and nuts can easily become 400+ calories.
common_mistakes: Oats are healthy but not automatically low-calorie. A loaded oats bowl can match a paratha breakfast.
visual_references: 1 bowl plain oats (water) = ~170 cal; with milk + toppings = ~350+ cal

fun_facts: Chicken breast has the best protein-to-calorie ratio of any food: 31g protein in just 165 calories.
100g of chicken breast gives you as much protein as 5 boiled eggs at fewer calories.
common_mistakes: Grilled vs fried chicken breast: 165 cal vs 215 cal per 100g. The cooking method adds 30%.
visual_references: 1 chicken breast = ~248 cal with 46g protein — the gold standard for protein

fun_facts: Moong sprouts at 50 cal/100g are one of the most nutrient-dense low-calorie foods available.
A full bowl of steamed sprouts (100 cal) has fewer calories than a single samosa.
common_mistakes: Steamed sprouts are 50 cal. Sprout chaat with oil can be 90 cal for the same amount. Preparation matters.
visual_references: 1 bowl steamed sprouts = ~100 cal — excellent volume food

fun_facts: Paneer bhurji has 18g protein per 100g — the best vegetarian protein option after paneer tikka.
Paneer bhurji vs egg bhurji: paneer has 70% more calories for similar protein. Eggs win on efficiency.
common_mistakes: It is high protein but also high fat. Paneer is 260 cal/100g vs chicken breast at 165 cal/100g.
visual_references: 1 katori paneer bhurji = ~312 cal with 22g protein

fun_facts: Brown rice has only 14% fewer calories than white rice — the difference is smaller than most people think.
The real benefit of brown rice is fiber (3x more than white), not calorie reduction.
common_mistakes: Switching from white to brown rice saves only 18 cal per 100g. It is not a magic weight loss food.
visual_references: 1 plate brown rice = ~224 cal vs white rice ~260 cal — modest difference

fun_facts: A grilled cheese sandwich can be 390 cal — similar to a plate of rajma chawal.
The bread contributes about 40% of a sandwich's calories. Open-face saves 80-100 cal.
common_mistakes: Grilling adds butter. A grilled sandwich is 20% more calories than a regular one.
visual_references: 1 regular sandwich = ~323 cal; grilled = ~390 cal

fun_facts: Fried chicken is 250 cal/100g vs grilled chicken breast at 165 cal/100g — batter adds 50% more calories.
3 pieces of fried chicken (600 cal) equals a full biryani plate.
common_mistakes: The batter and frying turn lean chicken into a calorie-dense food. The chicken inside is fine — it is the coating.
visual_references: 1 piece fried chicken = ~200 cal; tandoori leg piece = ~180 cal for more protein

fun_facts: Dal vada has better protein than most snacks because the base is lentils, not potatoes.
3 dal vadas (252 cal) have about the same calories as 1 samosa — but with double the protein.
common_mistakes: They are small so you eat many. 5 pieces is 420 calories.
visual_references: 1 dal vada = ~84 cal with 3g protein — better than most fried snacks
